## Round 38: TM-B40 (decision D-45)
This round fixes three related low-severity bugs:
- **Focus loss:** Done and Save Tags lose keyboard focus because they become natively `disabled`. The fix switches them to `aria-disabled` plus `aria-busy` and adds a click guard. Save Tags also used to lose focus after every successful save, because "nothing to save" disabled it too; that case is covered.
- **Faded arrows:** while Done is busy, the field-reorder arrows in the field editor were dimmed twice and ended up at about 18 % visibility.
- **Weak test check:** one test assertion could not tell the two re-reads apart; one line is added.

I built and tested the fix in a throwaway copy before writing the task:
- **jsdom does not reproduce the focus loss.** A focused button keeps focus there even after it becomes disabled. So the unit tests can only prove the attributes and the guard; focus itself is proven only by C's keyboard test in the real app, old build against new.
- **On the current code:** 30 of 304 tests fail. That is 7 of the 8 new tests (the eighth is a pin) and 23 existing tests that reach the 12 assertions being migrated to `aria-disabled`.
- **With the fix:** 304/304 pass, twice; type checks are clean; Biome shows 0 errors and the same 8 warnings; all 11 mutants are killed.
- **No doc refs move:** the new helpers sit at the end of their files, so every existing `docs/bugs/001` line ref up to `SchemaEditor.tsx:279` and `MetadataPanel.tsx:372` keeps its number.

I also added a note for C: Playwright treats `aria-disabled` buttons as disabled, so C must press keys on them rather than call `click()`, or the run will time out.

The references are the W3C ARIA keyboard guide and MDN `aria-disabled`, plus the round-35 sources. I found no desktop tag-editor source on this point and didn't invent one. Six deviations are listed with reasons.
